turns.assessment: The event is an abrupt, all-channel optical loss, not a service-specific failure: many unrelated services failed or switched protection simultaneously, and numerous S15 line interfaces raised OCH_LOS. The earliest localizing alarm is AMP_INPUT_LOS at amp1 on S01→S15, placing the break upstream of amp1; unchanged pump current across the amplifiers argues against a pump failure. The most likely cause is therefore a cut of span0 between amp0 and amp1, although the unchanged reverse direction means it is likely a single-fibre rather than the usual whole-cable cut.

proposals.rationale: A hard break in oms.S01-S15.span0 directly explains AMP_INPUT_LOS at downstream amp1 and the simultaneous loss of all channels and dependent services. Stable amplifier pump currents support a passive break after amp0. Reverse-direction stability is contrary to the usual two-fibre cable cut but does not exclude a single-fibre break.

Severe damage, a crushed cable, or a damaged splice on span0 could add enough loss to produce input and channel LOS while leaving amplifier pump currents unchanged, though the abrupt complete loss is more characteristic of a cut.

A disconnected OMS input patch at S01 would abruptly remove every S01→S15 channel and propagate LOS to amp1. It is less well localized than a span0 break, and recent S01 maintenance was several days earlier.
Failure of booster amp0 would remove the signal presented to amp1, but the unchanged amp0 pump-current telemetry is evidence against this mechanism.
